posts.linkedInPost:
🛠️ Building My Own Automated AI Content Manager — And the Bugs That Almost Made Me Give Up

For the past few weeks, I've been working on something I've always wanted: an AI-powered content manager that schedules posts, generates ideas, and tracks engagement across platforms.

The concept seemed straightforward:
📍 Feed it topics and let AI generate content variations
📍 Schedule posts across LinkedIn, Twitter, and other platforms
📍 Track performance and optimize based on engagement
📍 Learn from successful posts to improve future content

Everything was going smoothly until the bugs started piling up.

⸻

The AI Duplication Bug That Drove Me Crazy

My biggest headache? The AI kept generating nearly identical titles for completely different topics. I'd feed it "backend optimization" and "frontend performance," and somehow both would come out as "Optimizing Your Code: A Developer's Guide."

I spent 3 hours convinced it was a caching issue, checking Redis, clearing databases, even restarting the entire system.

Turns out, my prompt wasn't specific enough. I was asking for "engaging titles" without giving context about the unique angle each post should take.

The fix? Adding topic-specific constraints and example formats to each AI call. Simple, but it took me way too long to realize.

⸻

Scheduling Logic Gone Wrong

Another fun bug: posts were scheduling correctly but publishing at completely random times. A post meant for 9 AM was going live at 3 AM, ruining my engagement strategy.

The issue was timezone handling. I was storing UTC timestamps but not converting them properly for each platform's API requirements.

Lesson learned: always test timezone edge cases, especially when dealing with multiple APIs.

⸻

What's Working So Far

✅ Content generation with topic clustering
✅ Cross-platform posting (when timezone bugs aren't acting up)
✅ Basic engagement tracking
✅ Learning from high-performing content patterns

⸻

What Still Needs Work

🔄 Smarter AI prompts for unique content angles
🔄 Reliable timezone handling across all platforms
🔄 Better error handling when APIs go down
🔄 Content performance prediction based on historical data

⸻

The Real Challenge

Building this tool isn't just about the technical implementation — it's about understanding what makes content resonate. The AI can generate text, but it can't replicate authentic voice or genuine insights from experience.

That balance between automation and authenticity is what I'm still figuring out.

⸻

Next up: improving the AI's context awareness and building better failsafes for when things go wrong. Because they will go wrong.

Have you built anything with AI that surprised you with unexpected bugs? I'd love to hear your stories.
